title: Nova Programme
body_html:
Summary

Replace a manual, repetitive Long-Term Storage (LTS) release process with an automated, deterministic pipeline across 27 Vantage components.

Details

Client area: Acme Health, Clinical Systems, Vantage Platform
Our firm: Northwind
Duration: 12 weeks, fixed scope (charter v1.0, April 2026)
Effort: 124 days across 5 phases

One-line purpose

Replace a manual, repetitive Long-Term Storage (LTS) release process with an automated, deterministic pipeline.

Why it exists

The manual LTS process needed many fix-and-retry iterations per service and stretched LTS releases to 2-3 months. Goal: predictable, traceable releases with far less manual effort.

Approach in plain words

Two phases chained together:

  1. Promote dependencies based on a software bill of materials (SBOM).
  2. Run an LTS verification build per component, parse failures, auto-fix known failure types, stop safely (circuit breaker) when retries run out.

Fully deterministic. No AI/ML by design.

Scale

27 Vantage components in scope.

Phases and milestones

PhaseWeeksFocus
1 Foundation and requirements1-3Requirements, design, process analysis
2 LTS orchestrator pipeline4-8Pipeline build, SBOM, promotion, verification builds
3 Deterministic failure remediation9-10Log parsing, classification, auto-promotion, circuit breaker
4 Integration and testing11-12E2E tests, all 27 components, dashboards
5 Deployment and rollout12Rollout, docs, knowledge transfer, closure

Milestones M1 (wk 3) foundation, M2 (wk 8) pipeline ready, M3 and M4 (wk 10) remediation and pilot, M5 (wk 11) production ready, M6 (wk 12) full deployment and handover.

Success targets

  • 90% less manual dependency resolution
  • 80% of failures auto-remediated
  • 85%+ accuracy in automated artifact resolution
  • End state: Acme Health team runs pipeline independently

Out of scope (headline)

Artifact repository administration, microservice code changes beyond pipeline compatibility, AI/ML, replacing existing tooling.

Where the real detail lives

Not copied here on purpose. Open the program charter and the solution design below.

  • Ion Charter
  • Everest Design

Sign-off order

Northwind delivers, then Taylor Marsh (end user) signs off, then sponsor Shay Chandler gives final approval.

People

  • Project sponsor: Shay Chandler
  • Primary user: Taylor Marsh, in the Beacon Systems Navigators
  • Client users: Beacon Systems Navigators (users, including the primary user)
  • Product Manager, manages the microservice teams: Lane Underwood
  • Client owners of Vantage-dsl-lib and DevOps: Beacon Systems Rangers
  • Our team: Northwind Sentinels

Architecture: LTS release pipeline

What it is

An automated, deterministic pipeline that replaces the manual Long-Term Storage (LTS) release process for 27 Vantage components. No AI/ML by design.

Context diagram

mermaidflowchart LR
  SBOM[SBOM per component] --> P[Dependency promotion]
  P --> V[LTS verification build]
  V -->|pass| R[Release ready]
  V -->|fail| L[Log parsing and classification]
  L -->|known failure| F[Auto-fix / auto-promotion]
  F --> V
  L -->|unknown or retries exhausted| C[Circuit breaker: stop and alert]

Components

ComponentPurposeTechOwner
OrchestratorChains promotion and verification per componentTODONorthwind
Dependency promotionPromotes dependencies from the SBOMTODONorthwind
Verification buildRuns LTS build per componentTODONorthwind
Failure remediationParses logs, classifies failures, applies known fixesTODONorthwind
Circuit breakerStops safely when retries pass a thresholdTODONorthwind
DashboardsVisibility of runs and resultsTODONorthwind

Integrations

TODO: CI and source control, artifact repository.

Key design decisions

DecisionWhyDateApproved by
Fully deterministic, no AI/MLPredictable, traceable releases2026-04Charter v1.0
Design decisions reviewed by Acme SMEs before buildClient alignment2026-04Vantage LTS governance

Constraints

Out of scope: artifact repository administration, microservice code changes beyond pipeline compatibility, replacing existing tooling.

Source documents

  • Ion Charter: scope, phases, milestones, success targets.
  • Everest Design: architecture and design decisions.

Showcase

A healthcare technology company released long-term versions of its software platform by hand. Each of 27 components needed repeated fix-and-retry cycles, and one release took two to three months.

Northwind built an automated, deterministic release pipeline. It promotes dependencies from a software bill of materials, runs a verification build per component, classifies failures from the build logs, fixes known failure types automatically and stops safely when retries run out. There is no AI/ML, by design, so every release is predictable and traceable.

Targets: 90% less manual dependency resolution, 80% of failures fixed automatically, 85% or more accuracy in artifact resolution, and the client's own team running the pipeline after handover. A 12-week, fixed-scope engagement.

Ways of working

Cadence

  • Daily: internal standup (Teams) and an end-of-day email with three points: done, at risk or blocked, action needed.
  • Same-day blocker alert: sent to the blocker owner with description, impact, action, deadline. Escalates after 24 hours unresolved.
  • Weekly: engineering review with Acme Health team; Friday four-quadrant status report (accomplishments, in progress, risks and issues, next week).
  • Per milestone: summary email to stakeholders.

Escalation

  • Technical: program manager or engineering team, then Acme Health SMEs, then Acme Health Director.
  • Commercial or scope: program manager, then Northwind, then formal Change Request.

Rule of thumb

Design decisions go to Acme Health SMEs for alignment before implementation starts.
